Mr. Candy secretly gave Franklin Blake laudanum, planned as "five-and-twenty minims of laudanum tonight, without his knowing it." Godfrey Ablewhite dropped the dose into Blake's cold brandy and water before bed, as a practical joke to refute Blake's ridicule of medicine at the dinner.

The dead man was **Godfrey Ablewhite**. Sergeant Cuff pulled off his wig and beard and washed off his darkened complexion, and the name matched the one Cuff had written in his sealed letter: "_Godfrey Ablewhite_." This happened in a garret room at "The Wheel of Fortune" public-house in Shore Lane.

At the very end, Mr. Murthwaite sees the Moonstone gleaming in the forehead of the moon-god, which is seated on its antelope at a shrine on a hill near the sacred city of Somnauth, in Kattiawar, India. As he puts it, it "looks forth once more, over the walls of the sacred city in which its story first began."

It is **Mr. Septimus Luker**, of Middlesex Place, Lambeth, described as "the well-known dealer in ancient gems, carvings, intagli, &c." Godfrey Ablewhite pledged the Moonstone to him, and Luker deposited it with his bankers before handing it back on the day it was redeemed.

Sergeant Cuff loves talking about roses. He lectures the gardener on using "grass walks" instead of gravel and argues endlessly with Mr. Begbie about whether "the white moss rose" must be budded on the dog-rose.

Miss Clack carries tracts in her bag. She says she has "always a few tracts in my bag." One of them is "A Word With You On Your Cap-Ribbons," and another, on profane swearing, is titled "Hush, for Heaven's Sake!" On other occasions she also fills her carpet-bag with "precious publications," such as *The Serpent at Home*, to scatter about Lady Verinder's house.

Rosanna wrote that, being in love with Franklin Blake, she could not bear to destroy "the only thing I had which proved that I had saved you from discovery." She kept it as her one "claim on your confidence and your gratitude," something she could produce to make him trust her if they ever came to an explanation.
